method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 22 November, averaging 44.6 on Google's 0-100 scale, 5.4 times the next party (the Greens). That is 67% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 17.0 points (+62%).
Searches for the Greens jumped to 11 on 20 November, 2.1 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “Hadley: Stop Greens’ Aboriginal identity rort now” (The Daily Telegraph).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “mike newman”, “one nation ai ad”, “one nation bluey cartoon”.
victoria: 3 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 8 pollsters, the Coalition averages 31.8% of the primary vote, Labor 22.1%, One Nation 21.2% and the Greens 14.4%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 56.7 to 43.3 (6 polls), an 11.7-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (64 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (YouGov, 6–23 Nov 2026): Wilson 34%, Carroll 19%, Pickering 19%.
